queries.sql: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'In meeting the gross income test for claiming his father as a dependent, Doug considered the income received by his father. This income included gross rents of $4,000 (expenses were $2,000), municipal bond interest of $1,200, dividends of $1,400, and Social Security of $4,000. What is Doug\'s father\'s gross income for dependency test purposes?', '[\"$8,600\",\"$5,400\",\"$3,400\",\"$9,400\"]', 1, 'Answer : Option B is correct. To meet the gross income test, a person\'s gross income for the year must be less than $5,200 in 2025. Gross income is defined as all income in the form of money, property, and services that is not exempt from tax. In a manufacturing, merchandising, or mining business, gross income is the total net sales minus the cost of goods sold, plus any miscellaneous income from the business. In the case of rental property, gross receipts are gross income. Do not deduct taxes, repairs, etc. to determine the gross income from rental property. Gross income also includes all taxable unemployment compensation, taxable social security benefits, and certain scholarship and fellowship grants. Scholarships received by degree candidates that are used for tuition, fees, supplies, books, and equipment required for particular courses generally are not included in gross income. Tax-exempt income, such as certain Social Security payments, is not included in gross income. In this case, Doug\'s father has gross income for the dependency test purpose of $5,400, which is the sum of the rents ($4,000) and the dividend income ($1,400).', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Peter\'s unmarried daughter lived with him in his house for the entire year 2025. Peter owns the home and pays all the costs of upkeep for that home. His ex-wife did not live in the home at any time during the year. What is Peter\'s filing status for tax year 2025?', '[\"Head of household\",\"Married filing jointly\",\"Single\",\"Married filing separate\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. In order to qualify for head of household status, a taxpayer must meet all of the following requirements is unmarried or “considered unmarried” as of the last day of the year, paid more than half of the cost of maintaining a home for the year, and a qualifying person lived with the taxpayer in the home for more than half of the year (except for temporary absences, such as school). A taxpayer is considered unmarried if they satisfy all five tests which are: file a separate return, paid more than half the cost of keeping up the taxpayer\'s home for the tax year, the taxpayer\'s spouse did not live in the taxpayer\'s home during the last 6 months of the tax year, the taxpayer\'s home is the main home for the taxpayer\'s child, stepchild, or foster child for more than half the year, and the taxpayer must be able to claim an exemption for the child. (However, the taxpayer meets this test if they cannot claim the exemption only because the noncustodial parent can claim the child.) Given that Peter is unmarried and paid for all of the costs of maintaining the home, and his unmarried daughter lived with him for the entire year, he is eligible to file as head of household for 2025.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following items is an adjustment to income for a taxpayer in 2025?', '[\"State and local taxes\",\"Trade or business expenses\",\"IRA contribution\",\"Rent and royalty expense\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. Schedule 1 (Form 1040) provides a list of expenses that are Adjustments to Income. Some of those items include educator expenses, health savings account (HSA) deductions, moving expenses for members of the Armed Forces, SEP and SIMPLE contributions, IRA deductions, and student loan interest deductions. (Schedule 1 (Form 1040), page 1) In addition, the net amounts from rent and royalties, and trade and business are part of the total income calculation. Hence, they are Additional Income (or Losses). (Schedule 1 (Form 1040), page 1) State and local tax, on the other hand, is an itemized deduction that a taxpayer may claim if they itemize instead of taking the standard deduction. Thus, it is a deduction from adjusted gross income. (Schedule A (Form 1040), page 1) Hence, the only item that is an adjustment to income on Schedule 1(Form 1040) is an IRA contribution.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'John is the sole support of his mother. To claim her as a dependent on his Form 1040-SR for 2025, she must be a resident of which of the following countries for some part of calendar year 2025?', '[\"Mexico\",\"United States\",\"Canada\",\"United States, Mexico, or Canada\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits . Therefore, the following rules are provided: The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative . There are four tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative: Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) If a person is a qualifying relative, the person still must satisfy three additional tests: Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test expands on the citizen or residency test by stating, in part, that a taxpayer cannot claim an exemption for a dependent unless that person is a U.S. citizen, U.S. resident alien, U.S. national, or resident of Canada or Mexico. There is an exception for certain adopted children, which is not relevant to this problem. In this problem, John\'s mother can be a resident of any one of the three countries (United States, Mexico, or Canada) to qualify as his dependent.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'No estimated tax payments are required if enough tax is paid through withholding to keep the amount owed with the return:', '[\"to be $2,000 or less.\",\"to be $1,000 or less.\",\"to be under $1,000.\",\"to be under $2,000.\"]', 1, 'Answer: Option B is correct. In general, a taxpayer must pay estimated tax if both of the following apply: The taxpayer expects to owe at least $1,000 in tax for 2025 after subtracting his or her withholdings and refundable credits. The taxpayer expects his or her withholdings and credits to be less than the smaller of 90% of the tax to be shown on the 2025 tax return or 100% of the tax shown on the 2024 tax return. Moreover, the 2024 tax return must cover all 12 months. Remember, if a taxpayer\'s AGI for 2024 was more than $150,000 ($75,000 if married filing separately for 2024), then 110% is substituted for the 100% in the rule above.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Kathy, a U.S. citizen, is 22 years old and correctly files as single. In 2025, she had net self-employment income of $550 after expenses. She had no other income or any tax payments. Which of the following statements is correct concerning Kathy\'s requirement to file a federal income tax return for the year 2025?', '[\"Kathy is not required because she has does not have net earnings from self-employment in excess of the minimum filing amount.\",\"Kathy is required because she has net earnings from self-employment in excess of the minimum filing amount.\",\"Kathy is not required because she can be claimed on her parents\' return as a child.\",\"There is not enough information to respond to the question.\"]', 1, 'Answer:Option B is correct a taxpayer must file a return if the taxpayer\'s gross income is at least as much as the filing requirement amount for his or her filing status and age. In the case of a self-employed taxpayer, a second rule also applies for determining when to file. Specifically, a self-employed taxpayer must file Form 1040 and Schedule SE (Form 1040), Self-Employment Tax, if: the taxpayer\'s net earnings from self-employment (excluding church employee income) were $400 or more, or the taxpayer had church employee income of $108.28 or more. As a result, Kathy is required to file because she has net earnings from self-employment of $550, which exceeds the minimum filing amount of $400.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'What is the filing status of a taxpayer if their spouse died during the year?', '[\"Single\",\"Head of household\",\"Married filing jointly\",\"Qualifying surviving spouse\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. in part that a taxpayer is considered married for the whole year if, on the last day of the taxpayer\'s tax year, the taxpayer and the taxpayer\'s spouse meet any one of the following tests: married and living together, living together in a common-law marriage that is recognized in the state where the taxpayer now lives or in the state where the common-law marriage began, married and living apart, but not legally separated under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance, or separated under an interlocutory (not final) decree of divorce. In the case where a spouse died during the year, the taxpayer is considered married for the whole year for filing status purposes. Hence, the taxpayer would have a filing status of married jointly.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Filing Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, gives you:', '[\"a 6-month extension to file the tax return.\",\"an extension of time to pay the amount of taxes due.\",\"no interest on the amount due from the original due date of the return, which for most taxpayers is April 15.\",\"a penalty-free period of 6 months if you cannot pay the taxes due by the filing date.\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. in part, that if a taxpayer cannot file his or her tax return by the due date, the taxpayer may be able to get an automatic 6-month extension of time to file. However, failure to pay the tax due by the regular due date (generally, April 15) will result in the taxpayer owing interest on the tax liability and may also result in penalty charges for failing to file the return when due. A taxpayer can get the automatic extension by: Using IRS e-file (electronic filing), or Filing a paper form (i.e., Form 4868)', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'April is 18 years old and single. Her only income in 2025 was $600 of self-employment income from selling cosmetics. Which of the following statements is correct?', '[\"April is required to file a tax return in 2025 because she exceeded the gross income level for a single filer.\",\"April is not required to file a tax return in 2025 because she did not exceed the minimum self-employment income level.\",\"April is required to file a tax return in 2025 because she exceeded the minimum self-employment income level.\",\"April is not required to file a tax return in 2025 because she did not exceed the gross income level for a single filer.\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. a self-employed person must file a return if the taxpayer\'s gross income is at least as much as the filing requirement amount for his or her filing status and age. In April\'s case, she is required to file a tax return if her gross income was equal to or greater than $15,750. Although her gross income does not reach this plateau, there is another rule to consider for a self-employed taxpayer. A self-employed taxpayer must file Form 1040 and Schedule SE (Form 1040), Self-Employment Tax, if: the taxpayer\'s net earnings from self-employment (excluding church employee income) were $400 or more, or the taxpayer had church employee income of $108.28 or more. As a result of the above rules, April is required to file a tax return in 2025 because her minimum self-employment income exceeded the minimum reporting level.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Sue must make estimated tax payments of $4,000 for the tax year. She makes the following payments:', '[\"1st Payment\u2014credit of $1,000 from her previous year refund\",\"2nd Payment\u2014$500 on April 20\",\"3rd Payment\u2014$500 on May 31\",\"4th Payment\u2014$1,000 on August 15\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. For estimated tax purposes, the tax year is divided into four payment periods for taxpayers that are required to make estimated tax payments. Each period has a specific payment due date and if the taxpayer does not pay enough tax by the due date of each of the payment periods, then a penalty may be charged even if the taxpayer is due a refund when the income tax return is filed The specific payment dates for estimated tax payments are as follows: April 15, June 15, September 15, and finally January 15 of the following year. Per Publication 505, page 26, the regular installment method provides: \"if your first estimated tax payment is due April 15, you can figure your required payment for each period by dividing your annual estimated tax due by 4. (...) However, use this method only if your income is basically the same throughout the year.\" In this case, Sue made at least a $1,000 payment ($4,000 ÷ 4 periods) by each payment date. Hence, she has made timely estimated payments.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'In which of the following situations is no return required to be filed in 2025?', '[\"Single, filing status single, under age 65, gross income $16,000\",\"Married, separate filing status, age 65, gross income $6,000\",\"Single, filing status single, age 70, gross income $16,000\",\"Married, joint filing status, both spouses under age 65, gross income $32,000\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. the most comprehensive presentation on when a taxpayer must file a tax return. In this problem: The single person with a single filing status and age 65 or older (age 70 in this case) with gross income of $16,000 is not required to file a tax return because gross income is under $17,750. The single person with a single filing status and under age 65 with gross income of $16,000 is required to file a tax return because gross income is over $15,750. The married couple with a joint filing status and both spouses under age 65 with gross income of $32,000 is required to file a tax return because gross income is over $31,500. The married person with a separate filing status and any age (age 65 in this case) with gross income of $6,000 is required to file a tax return because gross income is over $5 in 2025. (Note the $5 threshold is not a typo!)', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Mr. and Mrs. Rose are both over 65. Their adjusted gross income is $100,000. During the year their 35-year-old single son, Tom, lived with them while attending college and earned $5,500. Mr. Rose\'s mother, Ivy, lived with them until June 1 when she was placed in a nursing home for an indefinite period to receive medical care. Ivy received no income and was supported solely by Mr. and Mrs. Rose. Determine the number of individuals (excluding themselves) that Mr. and Mrs. Rose can list on their Form 1040 as dependents on their 2025 joint return.', '[\"None\",\"2\",\"1\",\"4\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits. Therefore, the following rules are provided. The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative. There are four tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative : Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) To be a qualifying child, the child must be under age 19 (24 if a full-time student) and must satisfy both tests 2 and 4 above. In addition, a qualifying child is exempt from all of the above tests except the gross income test but be aware there are a number of exceptions to the above tests for a qualifying child . In this case, only Mr. Rose\'s mother, who is totally supported by the couple, can be listed on the taxpayer\'s tax return. Mr. Rose\'s mother is one of the relatives that does not need to live with the taxpayer to satisfy the relationship test. Hence, she qualifies as a dependent. Although Tom is a student, he does not qualify as a dependent under the qualifying child rules (age limit is exceeded). However, he may still qualify as a qualified relative. Since his gross income of $5,500 exceeds the gross income test limit of $5,200, he does not meet the requirements for a qualified relative either. Hence, he cannot be claimed as a dependent.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Don and Joyce have adjusted gross income of $85,000. Both children (Mary, age 14, and David, age 20, who completed his education in the prior year) lived with them all year. Mary had interest income of $300. David had interest income of $600 and wages of $6,500. The parents provided over 50% of the support of both children. How many dependents, not including Don and Joyce, would they list on their Form 1040 as dependents?', '[\"3\",\"2\",\"4\",\"1\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits. Therefore, the following rules are provided: The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative. There are four tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative: Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) To be a qualifying child, the individual must be under age 19 (24 if a full-time student) and must satisfy both tests 2 and 4 above. In addition, a qualifying child is exempt from all of the above tests except the gross income test. But, be aware there are a number of exceptions to the above tests for a qualifying child. If a person is a qualifying relative or a qualifying child, the person still must satisfy three additional tests Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test In this case, one dependent would be listed on Don and Joyce\'s Form 1040. Their daughter (Mary, age 14) qualifies as a dependent (meets the qualifying child test). David, on the other hand, does not qualify under qualifying child (he is 20 and not a full-time student). He can still qualify as a qualifying relative (no age test), but his gross income of $7,100 ($600 + $6,500) exceeds the gross income test limit of $5,200 for 2025.', 1)

INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'In meeting the “gross income” test for claiming his father as a dependent, the taxpayer had to consider the income received by his father. What is the father\'s gross income for dependency test purposes?', '[\"$11,600\",\"$8,400\",\"$9,600\",\"$2,000\"]', 1, 'Answer: Option B is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits. Therefore, the following rules are provided. The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative. There are four tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative: Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) If a person is a qualifying relative or a qualifying child, the person still must satisfy three additional tests: Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test gross income for the dependency test is all income in the form of money, property, and services that is not exempt from tax.
