timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following is the correct deadline for a taxpayer to obtain an automatic extension of time to file an individual tax return for 2025?', '[\"File Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, by April 1, 2026.\",\"File Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, by April 15, 2026.\",\"File Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, by June 1, 2026.\",\"File Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, by March 15, 2026.\"]', 1, 'Answer: Option B is correct. an automatic 6-month extension can be obtained by filing Form 4868 in paper form or by e-file by the due date for filing the taxpayer\'s tax return (generally, April 15). Form 4868 can be filed by mail up through April 15 by mailing it to the address shown in the form instructions. An extension does not abate any interest that is accruing for underpaying a person\'s income tax by the filing date. An extension also can be obtained by e-file by means of a person\'s personal computer or a tax professional providing certain information from the prior year’s tax form. An extension by e-file can be obtained by paying part or all of the taxpayer\'s estimated tax by use of a credit or debit card. The taxpayer can accomplish this by phone or over the Internet.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Mary\'s spouse died in 2022. Her son Bob is her dependent and has lived in her house since his birth in 2015. What is Mary\'s filing status in 2025 if she has not remarried?', '[\"Head of household\",\"Married filing jointly\",\"Single\",\"Qualifying surviving spouse\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. In general, if a taxpayer\'s spouse died in 2022, he or she can use the married filing jointly filing status for 2022. However, for the 2025 tax year and thereafter, the surviving spouse if not remarried is required to file as single unless he or she can qualify as a head of household. A surviving spouse may be eligible to file as a qualifying surviving spouse for 2 tax years following the year of death of their spouse, if the surviving spouse remains unmarried and maintains a household that, for the entire tax year, is the principal home of a son or daughter, adopted child, or stepchild for whom the taxpayer is entitled to the dependency exemption or could claim as a dependent except that for 2025 the child had gross income of $5,200 or more, the child filed a joint return, or the child could be claimed as a dependent on someone else’s return. A foster child does not make the surviving spouse eligible for the qualifying surviving spouse, but that does not mean that a surviving spouse cannot claim the foster child as a dependent. This benefit is afforded to a surviving spouse only if he or she was entitled to file a joint return with the deceased spouse during the year of death . As a result, in 2022, Mary was entitled to file a joint return for herself and her deceased husband. For 2023 and 2024, she was eligible to file as qualifying surviving spouse. For 2025 and thereafter, Mary would be eligible to file as head of household because she is unmarried on the last day of the year, paid more than half the cost of keeping up a home for the year, and has a qualifying person living with her in the home for more than half of the year', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following is true regarding the filing of Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return?', '[\"Filing Form 4868 provides an automatic 2-month extension of time to file and pay income tax.\",\"Electronic filing cannot be used to get an extension of time to file.\",\"Interest is charged on tax not paid by the due date of the return even if an extension is obtained.\",\"Any U.S. citizen who is out of the country on April 15, 2026, is allowed an automatic 6-month extension of time to file his\/her 2025 return and pay any federal income tax due.\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. an automatic 6-month (not 2-month) extension can be obtained by filing Form 4868 in paper form or e-filing. Form 4868 can be filed using e-filing up through April 15 by providing certain information from the prior year\'s tax form. A taxpayer can get an extension by paying part or all of their estimate of tax due by using a credit or debit card or by direct transfer from their bank account. A taxpayer can do this by phone or over the Internet. Under this method, a taxpayer does not file Form 4868. If an extension is obtained by the taxpayer, the return that was due on April 15, 2026, is now due on October 15, 2026. However, if the taxpayer does not pay the tax due by the regular due date (generally, April 15), the taxpayer will owe interest and may also be charged penalties.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Tyler is single and is 18 years old. He works part-time and is going to school. His total income for 2025 was $8,000. Tyler lives with his parents. He qualifies as their dependent and they are claiming him as a dependent on their 2025 tax return. Which of the following statements is correct with respect to claiming Tyler?', '[\"Only Tyler\'s parents can claim him as a dependent.\",\"Only Tyler can claim himself as a dependent.\",\"Either Tyler can claim himself as a dependent or Tyler\'s parents can claim him as a dependent.\",\"Neither Tyler can claim himself as a dependent nor can Tyler\'s parents claim him as a dependent.\"]', 0, 'Answer:Option A is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits . Therefore, the following rules are provided. The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative. There are five tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying child : Relationship Age Residency Support Joint return A qualifying child does not need to satisfy the gross income test (as in the case of a qualifying relative) unless the child fails to satisfy the age test. A child satisfies the age test if the child is: under age 19 at the end of the year, a full-time student under age 24 at the end of the year, or permanently and totally disabled at any time during the year, regardless of age. a person cannot claim any dependents, including themselves, if they can be claimed as a dependent by another person. Therefore, since Tyler qualified as a dependent to his parents, he cannot claim himself as a dependent. Only his parents can claim him as a dependent.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Michele is a member of the U.S. Armed Forces and served in an active status in a combat zone declared by executive order of the President from January 25, 2025, through March 17, 2025. She returned to the United States and received her regular duty pay for the rest of 2025. What portion of Michele\'s income is excluded on her Form W-2?', '[\"January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2025\",\"January 1, 2025, through March 31, 2025, only\",\"January 25, 2025, through March 17, 2025, only\",\"All of the income is taxable.\"]', 1, 'Answer:Option B is correct. gross income does not include compensation a person received for active service in the Armed Forces for any month during any part of which they served in a combat zone or qualified hazardous duty area. The exclusion available to person as a member of the Armed Forces may depend on their rank. An enlisted member, warrant officer, or commissioned warrant officer, can exclude the following amounts from income: Active duty pay earned in any month served in a combat zone. Imminent danger/hostile fire pay. A reenlistment bonus if the voluntary extension or reenlistment occurs in a month served in a combat zone. Pay for accrued leave earned in any month served in a combat zone. The DoD must determine that the unused leave was earned during that period. Pay received for duties as a member of the Armed Forces in clubs, messes, post and station theaters, and other non-appropriated fund activities. The pay must be earned in a month served in a combat zone. Awards for suggestions, inventions, or scientific achievements for submission made in a month served in a combat zone. The month for which the taxpayer received the pay must be a month in which the taxpayer either served in a combat zone or was hospitalized as a result of wounds, disease, or injury incurred while serving in the combat zone. The taxpayer does not have to receive the pay while in a combat zone, while he or she is hospitalized, or in the same year of service in a combat zone. Finally, if a person serves in a combat zone for any part of 1 or more days during a particular month, he or she is entitled to exclude the amount for that entire month. So, in this case, Michele could exclude from tax the income she earned in January, February, and March. The income she earned the rest of the year is not excludable as combat pay.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'John is an unmarried dependent child; he earns $16,000 wages during the summer, has no tips, has $200 in interest/dividends, and has no income tax withheld. Which of the following statements is correct with respect to him being required to file a tax return for 2025?', '[\"He is required to file a tax return because his unearned income exceeded the minimum amount.\",\"He is not required to file a tax return.\",\"He is required to file a tax return because his gross income exceeded the minimum amount.\",\"He is not required to file a tax return because his total income exceeded the minimum amount\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. a single dependent that is not age 65 or older or blind is required to file a tax return if any of the following apply: His or her unearned income was more than $1,350. His or her earned income was more than $15,750. His or her gross income was more than the larger of: $1,350 or his or her earned income (up to $15,750) plus $400. John is required to file a tax return for 2025 because he is an unmarried dependent child with gross income ($16,200) that exceeds $15,750.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'There are five tests that must be met for you to claim a qualifying relative as a dependent. Which of the following is not a requirement?', '[\"Joint return test\",\"Disability test\",\"Member of household or relationship test\",\"Citizen or resident test\"]', 1, 'Answer: Option B is correct. A taxpayer can claim one dependent for each person that satisfies the qualifying child or qualifying relative tests . There are four basic tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative : Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) If a person satisfies the above four tests under qualifying relative, he or she still must satisfy three additional tests : Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test The disability test is not one of the tests that must be met by a taxpayer to claim a qualifying relative as a dependent.', 1)

timelineData.name: Query
timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which one of the following criteria is used to determine a taxpayer\'s “tax home,” if the taxpayer does not have a regular or main place of business or work?', '[\"The taxpayer has not abandoned the area in which both his traditional place of lodging and his main home are located; members of his family live at his main home; or he often uses that home for lodging.\",\"The taxpayer performs part of his business in the area surrounding his main home and uses that home for lodging while doing business in the area.\",\"The taxpayer has living expenses at his main home that are duplicated because his business requires him to be away from that home.\",\"All of the answer choices are correct.\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. There are three factors that are used to determine the person\'s tax home if the taxpayer does not have a regular or main place of business or work: The taxpayer performs part of his or her business in the area of his or her main home and uses that home for lodging while doing business in the area. The taxpayer has living expenses at his or her main home that the taxpayer duplicates because the taxpayer\'s business requires the taxpayer to be away from that home. The taxpayer has not abandoned the area in which both the taxpayer\'s historical place of lodging and claimed main home are located; the taxpayer has a member or members of his or her family living at the main home; or the taxpayer often uses that home for lodging. In this problem, all three responses correspond to the above listed factors.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'In April 2025, 2 months after Tory and Wendy finished constructing a silo on their property, it was completely destroyed by a tornado. Their adjusted basis in the silo was its cost, $40,000. It was not covered by insurance. The entire community has been declared a qualified federal disaster area by the President. Tory and Wendy may elect to do which of the following?', '[\"Deduct $40,000 in either 2024 or 2025\",\"Deduct $40,000 in either 2025 or 2026\",\"Deduct $40,000 in 2024, 2025, or 2026\",\"No deduction in any year because the loss is personal\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. there are three types of casualty losses: A federal casualty loss is an individual’s casualty or theft loss of personal-use property that is attributable to a federally declared disaster. A disaster loss is a loss that is attributable to a federally declared disaster and that occurs in an area eligible for assistance pursuant to the Presidential declaration. A qualified disaster loss is an individual’s casualty or theft loss of personal-use property that is attributable to a major disaster declared by the President under section 401 of the Stafford Act in 2016 for a tax year designated by Congress as eligible for qualified disaster loss treatment, as well as other specified events. If you suffered a qualified disaster loss, you are eligible to claim a casualty loss deduction, to elect to claim the loss in the preceding tax year, and to deduct the loss without itemizing other deductions on Schedule A (Form 1040). If a taxpayer suffered a qualified disaster loss, they are eligible to claim the loss on the current tax year or amended return for the immediately preceding tax year. In such situations, the taxpayer is able to deduct the loss on the taxpayer\'s return or amended return for the tax year immediately preceding the tax year in which the disaster happened. If the person files an amended return, the loss is treated as having occurred in the preceding year. In this case, Tory and Wendy can deduct the entire loss of $40,000 in the current year or in the prior year by filing an amended tax return.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Lisa was married with two dependent children in 2025. Her husband died in April, and she did not remarry before the end of 2025. Which filing status should Lisa use for her tax return in 2025?', '[\"Head of household\",\"Qualifying surviving spouse\",\"Single\",\"Married filing jointly\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. a taxpayer is considered married for the whole year if, on the last day of the taxpayer\'s tax year, the taxpayer and the taxpayer\'s spouse meet any one of the following tests: married and living together, living together in a common-law marriage that is recognized in the state where the taxpayer now lives or in the state where the common-law marriage began, married and living apart, but not legally separated under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance, or separated under an interlocutory (not final) decree of divorce. In the case where a spouse died during the year, the taxpayer is considered married for the whole year for filing status purposes. Hence, Lisa is able to file as married filing jointly since her husband died during the current tax year. It should be noted that although Lisa may qualify under another filing status, married filing jointly is the most favorable tax filing status. Hence, Lisa should elect it, and that is the question here.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Brian is preparing his 2025 income tax return. He has gathered all of his records together for the current year, including a copy of the 2024 income tax return that he filed last year to assist with his preparation. While reviewing all of the forms he received for 2024 (i.e., Form W-2s and Form 1099s) he observes that his 2024 income tax return included dividends for ABC Corporation of $1,000 as reported on a 2024 Form 1099-DIV, but he does not have a 2025 Form 1099-DIV showing ABC Corporation dividends. Brian recalls that ABC Corporation has been paying an annual dividend for several years. Which of the following reasons could be why there is no Form 1099-DIV for ABC Corporation for 2025?', '[\"ABC Corporation may have paid a dividend in 2025 and the Form 1099-DIV is lost in the mail or the delivery has been delayed.\",\"Brian may have sold all of his shares in ABC Corporation in 2024 or 2025 after he was entitled to the 2024 dividend payment and before he was entitled to the 2025 dividend payment.\",\"ABC Corporation may not have paid a dividend for 2025.\",\"All of the reasons listed could be why there is no Form 1099-DIV for ABC Corporation for 2025.\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct.\nThere are six steps for preparing a tax return. The first two steps advise the taxpayer to get records together for income and expenses and to get the forms, schedules, and publications that are needed. These steps should be done before the income tax return is filled in.\nIn this case, Brian has made a useful observation while preparing his income tax return for 2025 that may not have occurred if he had not reviewed his 2025 income tax return and his basic records. ABC Corporation may not have paid a dividend in 2025, may have paid a dividend but the Form 1099-DIV is missing, or Brian may have sold it before he was entitled to a dividend in 2025. All of these reasons are possible. Thus, Brian should look further into why he did not receive the Form 1099-DIV. He may need to report dividends for 2025 or a sale or exchange of ABC stock in 2025 so that he can render a complete and accurate income tax return', 1)

Changes that should be reported include, but are not limited to, changes in household income; moving to a different address; gaining, losing, or other changes in employment; births or adoptions; marriage or divorce; and other changes affecting the composition of the taxpayer’s family.\nAs a result, all of the responses given are applicable. timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'To meet the dependency test of “gross income,” the taxpayer had to consider the following income received by his mother, who was 81 years of age: Social Security $3,600, municipal bond interest $2,200, corporate bond interest $1,300, stock dividends $900, rental income $1,500, rental expenses $200, and wages $600. The mother lived with the taxpayer the entire year. What is the correct gross income of the mother for this test?', '[\"$4,100\",\"$4,300\",\"$10,100\",\"$3,000\"]', 1, 'Answer: Option B is correct. To meet the gross income test, a person\'s gross income for the year must be less than $5,200 in 2025. Gross income is all income in the form of money, property, and services that is not exempt from tax. In a manufacturing, merchandising, or mining business, gross income is the total net sales minus the cost of goods sold, plus any miscellaneous income from the business. In the case of rental property, gross receipts are gross income. Do not deduct taxes, repairs, etc. to determine the gross income from rental property. Gross income also includes all taxable unemployment compensation, taxable Social Security benefits, and certain scholarship and fellowship grants. Tax-exempt income, such as tax-exempt income or untaxable Social Security payments, is not included in gross income. To determine whether Social Security benefits are taxable, the sum of one half of Social Security benefits ($1,800) and all the other income, including tax exempt income ($6,500) must not exceed $25,000 for a single person (Publication 915, page 3). Since the amount of $8,300 does not exceed $25,000, none of the Social Security benefits are taxable. As such, they will not be included in the computation of gross income for purposes of income testing associated with a qualifying relative. In this problem, the taxpayer\'s mother\'s gross income consisted of corporate bond interest, stock dividends, gross rental income, and wages or $4,300 ($1,300 + $900 + $1,500 + $600). Note that the $200 of rental expenses does not reduce the gross income figure.', 1)

timelineData.name: Query
timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following information does not appear on a paper Form 1040?', '[\"Dependent\'s date of birth\",\"Dependent\'s Social Security number\",\"Dependent\'s relationship to taxpayer\",\"All of the answer choices appear on Form 1040.\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. Form 1040 requires certain information concerning those individuals for whom a taxpayer is claiming them as dependents. In particular, a taxpayer must provide the dependent\'s first and last name, Social Security number, and the relationship to the taxpayer. In addition, a checkbox is given to indicate if the child qualifies for the child tax credit or a credit for other dependents. Although the date of birth for a dependent is not provided on Form 1040, it is necessary for a tax advisor to inquire about and obtain reasonable evidence about all dependents\' ages. Otherwise, it is questionable as to whether the person qualifies as a child or relative. Hence, in this case, the dependent\'s date of birth is not a line on a taxpayer\'s Form 1040. It is required to e-file a return as the computer determines what the taxpayer qualifies for based on the dependents\' age.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Mary\'s spouse, John, died in an auto accident in 2024. She has not remarried, and she supported their 5-year-old son all year. What is Mary\'s filing status for year 2025?', '[\"Qualifying surviving spouse\",\"Married filing separately\",\"Married filing jointly\",\"Single\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. In the case where a spouse dies, the surviving spouse has a filing status of married joint for the year of death. Thus, Mary would have a filing status of married joint for her 2024 tax year. For the 2 years following the death of the spouse (2025 and 2026), the surviving spouse may be eligible to use the qualifying surviving spouse status. This filing status entitles the surviving spouse to use the joint return tax rates and the highest standard deduction amount (if the taxpayer elects not to itemize deductions). This status does not entitle the surviving spouse to file a joint return. A taxpayer must meet all of the following tests in order to file their 2025 return as a qualifying surviving spouse: The taxpayer was entitled to file a joint return with their spouse for the year their spouse died. It does not matter whether the taxpayer actually filed a joint return. The taxpayer’s spouse died in 2023 or 2024 and the taxpayer did not remarry before the end of 2024. The taxpayer had a child or stepchild (not a foster child) whom they can claim as a dependent or could claim as a dependent except that for 2025: the child had gross income of $5,200 or more, the child filed a joint return, or the taxpayer could be claimed as a dependent on someone else’s return. This child lived in the taxpayer\'s home all year, except for temporary absences. The taxpayer paid more than half of the cost of keeping up a home for the year. Mary, in this case, has a filing status of qualifying surviving spouse because she has met all the tests listed above in 2025, which is the year following John\'s death.', 1)

Which of the following statements is correct with respect to him being required to file a tax return for 2025?', '[\"He is not required to file a tax return.\",\"He is required to file a tax return because his earned income exceeded the minimum amount.\",\"He is required to file a tax return because his total income exceeded the minimum amount.\",\"He is required to file a tax return because his unearned income exceeded the minimum amount.\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. a single dependent that is not age 65 or older or blind is required to file a tax return if any of the following apply: His or her unearned income was more than $1,350. His or her earned income was more than $15,750. His or her gross income was more than the larger of: $1,350 or his or her earned income plus $400 up to the regular standard deduction. John is not required to file a tax return for 2025 because he is an unmarried dependent child with earned income ($4,500) that does not exceed $15,750 and unearned income ($200) that does not exceed $1,350.', 1)

For a person to be able to file as head of household, the taxpayer must meet all of the following requirements: Be unmarried or “considered unmarried” on the last day of the year, Pay more than half the cost of keeping up a home for the year, and Have a “qualifying person” live with the taxpayer in the home for more than half the year (except for temporary absences, such as school). timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following is the green card test?', '[\"Whether or not income tax returns are filed using Certified Mail Return Receipt Requested (the green cards at the U.S. Post Office)\",\"Whether or not a taxpayer is a U.S. citizen at any time during calendar year 2025\",\"Whether or not a taxpayer is a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time during calendar year 2025\",\"None of the answer choices describe the green card test\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. A person is a resident alien of the United States for tax purposes if they meet either the green card test or the substantial presence test for the calendar year. Even if the person does not meet either test, they may be able to choose to be treated as a U.S. resident for part of the year. A person is a resident for tax purposes if they are a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time during the calendar year. This is known as the “green card” test. A taxpayer is a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time if they have been given the privilege, according to the immigration laws, of residing permanently in the United States as an immigrant. A taxpayer has this status if the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) (or its predecessor organization) has issued the taxpayer an alien registration card, also known as a “green card.” a resident alien’s income is generally subject to tax in the same manner as a U.S. citizen. Resident aliens must report all income from sources within and outside the United States. A nonresident alien usually is subject to U.S. income tax only on U.S. source income. In this case, whether or not a taxpayer is a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time during calendar year 2025 is the green card test. Mailing income tax returns to the Internal Revenue Service using the Certified Mail Return Receipt Requested at the U.S. Post Office is a good idea to prove timely filing and receipt of the income tax returns, but it is not the green card test.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Jill and John, married filing jointly, have provided more than 50% of the support for two minor children and Jill\'s mother. The children each had interest income of less than $1,000. Jill\'s mother received a taxable pension of $3,500, dividends of $1,500 and interest of $1,000. How many dependents can the taxpayers, excluding themselves, list on their 2025 tax return?', '[\"None\",\"1\",\"2\",\"3\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits. Therefore, the following rules are provided. The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative. There are four tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative : Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) Gross income is all income in the form of money, property, and services that is not exempt from tax. To be a qualifying child, the child must be under age 19 (24 if a full-time student) and must satisfy both tests 2 and 4 above. In addition, a qualifying child is exempt from all of the above tests except the gross income test but be aware there are a number of exceptions to the above tests for a qualifying child. If a person is a qualifying relative or a qualifying child, the person still must satisfy three additional tests: Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test More specifically, the gross income test generally will not allow a taxpayer to claim a dependent if that person had gross income of $5,200 or more for 2025. Given that Jill\'s mother\'s gross income ($6,000) is greater than the $5,200 limit Jill and John are unable to claim her as a dependent. Gross income calculation for Jill\'s mother: Thus, the couple would only claim two dependents, one for each minor child.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'John and Joanne are the sole support of the following individuals, all U.S. citizens, none of whom lives with them. None of these individuals files a joint return or has any gross income:', '[\"Jennie, John\'s mother\",\"Julie, Joanne\'s stepmother\",\"Jonathan, father of John\'s first wife\",\"How many individuals, excluding John and Joanne, are listed on their tax return for 2025 as dependents?\"]', 1, 'Answer: Option B is correct. For 2025, a taxpayer cannot claim a personal exemption deduction for themselves, their spouse, or their dependents. However, dependents are still listed on Form 1040 in order to claim appropriate tax credits . Therefore, the following rules are provided: The term “dependent” means a qualifying child or a qualifying relative. There are four tests that must be met for a person to be a qualifying relative : Not a qualifying child Member of the household or satisfies the relationship test Gross income test (less than $5,200 in 2025) Support test (more than half of the person\'s total support for the year) If a person is a qualifying relative or a qualifying child, the person must satisfy three additional tests to claim an exemption for him or her: Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test An exception exists to the Member of the Household rule. In particular, a person related to the taxpayer in any of the following ways does not have to live with the taxpayer for the entire year as a member of the taxpayer\'s household to meet this test : Child, grandchild, great-grandchild, etc. (a legally adopted child is considered your child), Stepchild, foster child, Brother, sister, half-brother, half-sister, stepbrother, or stepsister, Parent, grandparent, or other direct ancestor, but not foster parent, Stepfather or stepmother, Brother or sister of the taxpayer\'s father or mother, Son or daughter of the taxpayer\'s brother or sister, or Father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, brother-in-law, or sister-in-law. Better yet, any of these relationships that were established by marriage are not ended by death or divorce. As a result of the new tax, John and Joanne can claim three dependents on their return because the three individuals do not need to live with the taxpayer in order to be claimed as a dependent.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'George is preparing his income tax return for 2025 and believes that his itemized deductions will exceed his standard deduction. To what sources could George turn to see which deductions are applicable to him and how much he can deduct?', '[\"Cash receipts\",\"Financial account statements, checkbooks, canceled checks, and substitute checks\",\"Credit card statements\",\"All of the answer choices are correct\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. Taxpayers should itemize deductions if their total deductions are more than their standard deduction amount. Generally, a taxpayer may benefit from itemizing their deductions if they have such items as large uninsured medical and dental expenses, interest and taxes on their home, or large contributions to qualified charities. He has been divorced from his wife since March 1 of the tax year. They have two minor children. One child lives with Milton, and the other child lives with the mother. The children have been with their respective parents from March through December of the tax year. Milton provides all of the support for the minor child living with him. The filing status with the lowest rate that Milton qualifies for is:', '[\"married filing separately.\",\"single.\",\"married filing jointly.\",\"head of household.\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. Milton will qualify as head of household because he satisfies all of the requirements : unmarried or considered unmarried (generally, the taxpayer’s spouse did not live in the taxpayer’s home during the last 6 months of the tax year) on the last day of the year, paid more than half the cost of keeping up a home for the year, and a qualifying person lived with the taxpayer in the home for more than half the year (except for temporary absences, such as school). There is another exception to the third requirement; a taxpayer\'s dependent parents do not need to live with the taxpayer. Of course, this exception is not relevant to this problem. A taxpayer is considered unmarried if they satisfy all five tests, which are: file a separate return, paid more than half the cost of keeping up the taxpayer\'s home for the tax year, the taxpayer\'s spouse did not live in the taxpayer\'s home during the last 6 months of the tax year, the taxpayer\'s home is the main home for the taxpayer\'s child, stepchild, or foster child for more than half the year, and the taxpayer must be able to claim an exemption for the child. Since Milton is considered unmarried at year-end (i.e., divorced), has one child living with him, and paid more than half of the cost of keeping up a home for the year, he has satisfied all three conditions for claiming head of household filing status.', 1)

Tom was unable to work in 2025 because of a medical condition but received $5,500 from a charitable foundation for a speaking engagement. Which of the following statements is correct with respect to claiming Tom as a dependent on their tax return?', '[\"Ted and Sharon may claim Tom as a dependent on their 2025 federal income tax return or Tom may claim an exemption for himself on his 2025 federal income tax return.\",\"Ted and Sharon may claim Tom as a dependent on their 2025 federal income tax return.\",\"Tom cannot be claimed as a dependent on his parents\' 2025 federal income tax return and will need to file his own return.\",\"Tom cannot be claimed by either himself or his parents.\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. In addition, a qualifying child is exempt from all of the above tests except the gross income test . If a person is a qualifying relative, he or she still must satisfy three additional tests: Dependent taxpayer test Joint return test Citizen or resident test In this case, Tom is not a qualifying child because he is over the age of 19. Denise is a U.S. citizen and, except for the 3 months spent in Russia, resides in Mobile, Alabama. Denise did not receive either a Form W-2 or a Form 1099 for her earnings while in Russia. timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Reba, age 88, and Charles, age 90, are married, live together, and file jointly. During 2025, they received interest income of $6,000, dividend income of $1,500, a pension of $15,000, and Social Security of $17,000. Which of the following statements is correct?', '[\"The couple must include $8,500 of their Social Security benefits in gross income.\",\"Reba and Charles are required to file a tax return.\",\"Reba and Charles are not required to file a tax return.\",\"The couple does not include any Social Security benefits in gross income because they are over age 80.\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. a couple with a married joint filing status is not required to file a tax return where both spouses are 65 or older and gross income is less than $34,700, where one spouse is age 65 or older and gross income is less than $33,100, or where neither spouse is 65 or older and gross income is less than $31,500. some Social Security benefits become taxable if one-half of the benefits plus all other income, including tax-exempt interest, exceed the base amount of $32,000 in the case of a couple filing married ($25,000 if filing single or head of household and $0 if married, filing separate, and living with one\'s spouse at any time during 2025). Reba, age 88, and Charles, age 90, are married, live together, and file jointly. None of the Social Security benefits are included in gross income because the sum of AGI without the Social Security ($22,500) and one-half of the Social Security ($8,500) equals $31,000, which is less than the starting point of $32,000 for including Social Security income in gross income. Furthermore, the couple is not required to file a tax return because they had an AGI of $22,500, which is less than $34,700, in 2025. Thus, the correct response is that the couple is not required to file a tax return.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Phil is unmarried and his dependent daughter, Susan, lived with him all year. Property taxes of $2,500 and mortgage interest of $5,000 on the home where he and Susan live are divided equally with his ex-wife. Phil paid the utilities of $200 per month. What amount may Phil use as the costs of keeping up a home to qualify for head of household filing status?', '[\"$9,900\",\"$4,950\",\"$6,150\",\"$3,750\"]', 2, 'Answer: Option C is correct. To qualify for head of household status, a taxpayer must pay more than half of the cost of keeping up a home for the year. if a taxpayer satisfies this rule. Costs that are included are items in the cost of keeping up a home such as rent, mortgage interest, real estate taxes, home insurance, repairs, utilities, and food eaten in the home. Costs that are not included are items such as clothing, education, medical treatment, vacations, life insurance, or transportation. In addition, a taxpayer does not include the rental value of a home owned by the taxpayer, or the value of the taxpayer\'s services or those of a member of the taxpayer\'s household. In this case, Phil has upkeep costs of $6,150, which is the sum of his share of the property taxes ($1,250) and the mortgage interest ($2,500), and the full cost of the utilities ($2,400, or $200 per month times 12 months). Note: This question is tricky because the utilities are a monthly cost and the mortgage and taxes are given as an annual cost. Thus, you need to read carefully.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following statements is correct concerning the Additional Medicare Tax?', '[\"A taxpayer may claim a credit for any withheld Additional Medicare Tax against the total tax liability on their tax return by filing Form 8959.\",\"A nonresident alien is required to pay Additional Medicare Tax if their wages exceed the threshold amount.\",\"A taxpayer may be subject to a penalty for failure to make estimated tax payments if they owe Additional Medicare Tax.\",\"All of the responses are correct.\"]', 3, 'Answer:Option D is correct. As provided in the instructions for Form 8959, page 1, all wages that are subject to Medicare tax are subject to Additional Medicare Tax to the extent they exceed the threshold amount for a person’s filing status. The threshold for a married taxpayer filing jointly is $250,000 and for all other taxpayers is $200,000. However, the rules further state that employers must withhold Additional Medicare Tax on wages it pays to their employee in excess of $200,000 for the calendar year, regardless of the employee’s filing status and regardless of wages or compensation paid by another employer. As a result, an employee who has wages between $200,000 and $250,000 has Additional Medicare Tax withheld from their wages even though they are not subject to this tax if they file married jointly with their spouse who does not have any wages in that year. In this case, the taxpayer may claim a credit for any withheld Additional Medicare Tax against the total tax liability on their tax return by filing Form 8959. Second, a taxpayer may be subject to a penalty for failure to make estimated tax payments if they owe Additional Medicare Tax and wait to pay the tax with their tax return. (Form 8959, page 2) Third, a nonresident alien or a U.S. citizen living abroad is required to pay Additional Medicare Tax on Medicare wages, railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation, and self-employment income that exceed the threshold amount for the person\'s filing status. There are no special rules for nonresident aliens and U.S. citizens living abroad.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Rev. Elvin Snider is the ordained minister at Crossroads United Methodist Church. His salary on his Form W-2 is $20,000. He also receives a $12,000 housing allowance. His housing costs for the year are $14,000. What is Rev. Snider\'s self-employment income?', '[\"$32,000\",\"$34,000\",\"$20,000\",\"None of the answer choices are correct.\"]', 0, 'Answer: Option A is correct. all wages and self-employment income are subject to either SECA (Self-employment Contribution Act) or FICA (Federal Insurance Contribution Act). a minister is not covered by FICA but is covered under SECA – meaning is subject to self-employment taxes. Page 3 further provides: “if you are a member of a church, your earnings for the services you perform in your capacity as a minister are subject to SE tax, even if you perform these services as an employee of that church.” Ministers are individuals who are duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed by a religious body constituting church or church denomination. Furthermore, even though all of the income from performing ministerial services is subject to self-employment tax for social security purposes, you may be an employee for income tax or retirement plan purposes, in which case your income is considered wages and not self-employed income. a member of the clergy (minister, member of a religious order etc.) can request an exemption from self-employed tax. Provided that the clergy member meets the conditions they would start by filing Form 4361. a member of the clergy must include in income offerings and fees received for marriages, baptisms, funerals, masses, etc., in addition to the taxpayer\'s salary. If the offering is made to the religious institution and not the minister, the amount is not taxable to the minister. In addition to salary, special rules for housing apply to members of the clergy. Under these rules, a minister does not include in income the rental value of a home (including utilities) or a designated housing allowance that is provided to the minister. The exclusion, however, cannot be more than the lesser of the following amounts: The amount actually used to provide or rent a home; The fair market rental value of the home (including furnishings, utilities, garage, etc.); The amount officially designated (in advance of payment) as a rental or housing allowance; or An amount that represents reasonable pay for the taxpayer\'s service. The home or allowance must be provided as compensation for the minister\'s services as an ordained, licensed, or commissioned minister. However, the taxpayer must include the rental value of the home or the housing allowance as earnings from self-employment on Schedule SE (Form 1040) if the minister is subject to the self-employment tax. Rev. Snyder in this case would include $32,000, which is the sum of his W-2 income of $20,000 and his housing allowance of $12,000.', 1)

timelineData.query: INSERT INTO `tbl_unit_questions` (`unit_test_id`, `question_text`, `options`, `correct_option`, `explanation`, `is_active`) VALUES ('2', 'Which of the following situations will disqualify a single individual from claiming the premium tax credit?', '[\"Marriage to an individual enrolled in a qualified health plan\",\"Increase in household income to 390% of the federal poverty line\",\"Inheritance of $1,100,000 received during the tax year\",\"Becoming eligible as a dependent on their parent\'s joint tax return\"]', 3, 'Answer: Option D is correct. a taxpayer can take the premium tax credit (PTC) for 2025 if the taxpayer for at least 1 month of the year, meets all of the following: An individual in the taxpayer’s tax family was enrolled in a qualified health plan offered through the Marketplace on the first day of the month; and That individual was not eligible for minimum eligible coverage (MEC) for the month, other than individual market coverage; and The portion of the enrollment premiums for the month for which the taxpayer is responsible was paid by the due date of their tax return (not including extensions). In addition, The applicable taxpayer’s household income is at least 100% of the federal poverty line for their family, with no upper limit for 2025; and No one can claim the taxpayer as a dependent on a tax return for 2025; and If married by the end of the year, they must generally file a joint tax return. Since cash inheritances are not counted, the correct response for this question is that the individual cannot become eligible as a dependent on their parent’s tax return.', 1)
